blocks: ### T01 - the counter-only delta and the cohort skip (D1, D2)
### T02 - the claims triage's counter-only clear (D3)
### T03 - the docs and the report (D4)

decisions.summary: codeid.is_counter_block / _counter_value / strip_counters / debug_free_bytes as FR-001 defines them; the 3 non-counter if __debug__ blocks (BY_STAGE) stay code
decisions.why: Restates FR-001 and makes no choice it leaves open; the 136/133/3 figure carries a date and method (one-shot label). Serves the request's 'the proof mechanical, never a judgment'.

decisions.summary: counter_only walks cohort_known's ENGINE_PATHS, not land.py's ENGINE as FR-002 names
decisions.why: FR-002 fixes the set: 'every engine path it changes (land.py's ENGINE)'. D2 walks ENGINE_PATHS and nothing in the blocks says the two are one set. counter_only is 'every changed path in the list is counter-only-equal', which is vacuously true when the list names none of the changed files, so any path in land.py's ENGINE missing from ENGINE_PATHS can be rewritten and the landing still judged counter-only, skipping both cohorts - the case the GM's accepted change keeps them for ('Any landing that moves a map ... keeps both', 'the proof mechanical, never a judgment'). Whether the lists are identical is an unmeasured premise the plan does not state. Fix: D2 walks land.py's ENGINE, or states (and a test pins) that ENGINE_PATHS is that same object, imported, not a second list.

decisions.summary: only modifications count; an add, delete or rename of an engine path is never counter-only
decisions.why: FR-001's last sentence (an added or deleted file is never counter-only-equal); a rename failing the test is conservative and runs the cohorts.

decisions.summary: same_key returns True when counter_only does, after its two existing tests; delta.engine_key untouched
decisions.why: FR-002 verbatim: main's record stays the baseline so the next landing's cohort is not pushed onto it.

decisions.summary: new cohort_gate.py counter-only command (exit 0 when counter-only), delta against the merge base with origin/main; land.py then starts no cohort-landing and no fresh block and prints the skip
decisions.why: FR-002: base is the merge base with origin/main, make land skips both cohorts and 'says so'. Request change 1 names both the landing cohort and the fresh post-push block.

decisions.summary: claims triage: base unit fingerprinted through the same scan, equal to the recorded code; counter-free cores compared and the base's counter blocks standing in the current unit; cleared with current fingerprints and note 'counter-only (feature 446)', bundled nowhere
decisions.why: FR-003 and request change 2. 'Standing' must mean unchanged, as FR-003 says ('every counter block of the base version standing unchanged'; 'removed or rewritten' is owed). Non-blocking: T02's exits test a removed base counter block but not a rewritten one; the author should add that case.

decisions.summary: docs/guards.md cohort-gate and claims-gate rows and make land's help name the skips; feature report
none; claims scan gains a counter-free dump only for units owed a code triage
decisions.why: Tooling only; no roll code changes. Decides nothing the request constrains.

decisions.summary: tests: cohorts skipped on counter-only, run otherwise, full suite on both; each skip red with its condition deleted; claims cleared/owed cases
decisions.why: Enforcement of FR-002, FR-003, FR-004 and FR-005 - the kept full suite and the skips' guards - not scope.

decisions.summary: full suite, reviews, checklists, claims switch refusal unchanged
decisions.why: FR-004 and the request's 'Kept unchanged' list.

decisions.summary: One counter-block definition in codeid (is_counter_block, _counter_value, strip_counters, debug_free_bytes) as FR-001 defines it; the 3 BY_STAGE blocks stay code.
decisions.why: Implements FR-001 as written, including FR-001's own statement that the driver's BY_STAGE attribution is code; it serves change 1's 'the proof mechanical, never a judgment'.

decisions.summary: counter_only(root,a,b) over the engine paths named by land.py's ENGINE (moved to codeid.ENGINE, one definition both read, a test failing if they differ); adds/deletes never counter-only; same_key True when counter_only; land.py asks cohort_gate.py counter-only against the merge base and skips cohort-landing and the fresh block, printing the skip.
decisions.why: The previous round's finding is resolved: the engine list is now FR-002's own (land.py's ENGINE), and moving it to one shared definition is a refactor that cannot make the set differ. Merge base with origin/main, both cohorts skipped, the skip printed, same_key widened, engine_key untouched (not named as changed), adds/deletes excluded per FR-001 - all as FR-002 and change 1 state. Any other engine delta runs both cohorts.

decisions.summary: Where a claim's code changed, fingerprint the unit at the merge base; when it equals the recorded code and the counter-stripped cores are equal with the base's counter blocks standing in the current unit, record the claim cleared ('counter-only (feature 446)') with its current fingerprints, bundled nowhere.
decisions.why: Implements FR-003 and change 2. The 'standing' condition is FR-003's 'every counter block of the base version standing unchanged', and T02's exit now tests the rewritten-block case as well as the removed one, so the condition is enforced rather than paraphrased. The claims switch's refusal of an owed claim (FR-004) is not touched.

decisions.summary: docs/guards.md cohort-gate and claims-gate rows and make land's help name the skips.
decisions.why: FR-005's documentation clause, nothing more.

decisions.summary: Each skip tested to still run on a non-counter delta, red with its condition deleted; land.py test asserts the full suite on both deltas.
decisions.why: Enforcement of FR-005 and FR-004 (the full suite kept on every engine landing); serves the request.

decisions.summary: make feature-report F=446 WRITE=1 as the last task's exit.
decisions.why: Standard closing of a feature; adds no behavior and narrows nothing.

blocks: ### T01 - the counter-only delta and the cohort skip (D1, D2)

decisions.summary: T01 builds codeid's counter-block functions with tests, cohort_known.counter_only, same_key's third test, cohort_gate.py counter-only, and land.py skipping both cohorts on a counter-only delta
decisions.why: Each item is named by D1/D2 (FR-001, FR-002) and serves accepted change 1: skip the landing cohort and the fresh block after the push when a landing provably, mechanically moves no map. Skipping BOTH cohorts matches the request's 'keeps both' / skip both.

decisions.summary: Goal: a landing that only adds counters rolls no cohort; any other rolls both
decisions.why: Restates FR-002 in plain words, using the request's own 'gained counter lines' wording. The mechanism the task implements is D1/D2 cited in full (counter-only-equal), not a narrower rule; 'any other rolls both' is FR-002's 'Any other engine delta runs both cohorts as today'.

decisions.summary: Constraints FR-001, FR-002, FR-004, D1, D2; FR-004 keeps the full suite on every engine landing
decisions.why: The request keeps the full suite on every engine landing; the land.py exit test asserts the full suite runs on both counter-only and other deltas, enforcing that kept item.

decisions.summary: Green exits: test_codeid.py, a same_key test (counter-only successor same engine, an added file not), a land.py test (skip on counter-only, run on other, full suite on both), each skip red with its condition deleted; red exit records and sets down, a cannot-be-done claim goes to make arbiter-ask
decisions.why: Tests that only enforce the requested skip and its mechanical proof (FR-005, SC-001, SC-002, SC-004); the added-file case enforces FR-001's 'an added or deleted file is never counter-only-equal'. Enforcement of the request, not unrequested scope.

decisions.summary: Order first; budget one landing; done when a counter-only landing prints the skip and the push's cohort gate passes it
decisions.why: Sequencing and the done-measure restate D2's printed message and same_key acceptance by the push gate; the GM asked for this work to be prioritized so later landings are faster.

decisions.summary: 133 of 136 if __debug__ blocks under l7r/ are counter blocks, measured 2026-10-28 by an AST walk through is_counter_block
decisions.why: A one-shot labeled measurement (date and method) matching D1's recorded census; it decides no scope, only confirms the rule describes the code.

blocks: ### T02 - the claims triage's counter-only clear (D3)

decisions.summary: T02 runs after T01 because it reads T01's strip_counters
decisions.why: Sequencing only; D3 names strip_counters, which FR-001/T01 supplies. Narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: Green exit: test_claims_index.py clears a claim whose unit only gained a counter block, and owes a claim changed otherwise, one whose counter block was removed, one rewritten, and one whose recorded version is not the base's; the clear goes red with its condition deleted
decisions.why: Each case is FR-003's own clear and its four owed-as-today exclusions, and the condition-deleted red is FR-005/SC-003. This is enforcement of request change 2 (counter-only claims cleared mechanically, nothing else cleared), not added scope.

decisions.summary: Red exit: record what failed, set the task down, and route a claim that it cannot be done through make arbiter-ask
decisions.why: Standing process for a failed task; it does not relax FR-003 and keeps the round arbiter the request lists as kept.

decisions.summary: Done when a counter-only change's claims are cleared at make claims-owed with no bundle
decisions.why: That is FR-003's outcome (cleared, bundled nowhere) observed at claims_owed, one of the two entry points FR-003 names; the test exit covers the triage logic itself. Does not narrow the clear to one path - D3 places it in the shared code-triage owing.
